_comment: The next command each completed stage hands to. Read by `review_render.footer`, so a stage's successor is data rather than a sentence in fourteen files. Keys are `<workflow>.<stage>.<outcome>`; `lib/next_steps.resolve` also accepts a bare `<stage>.<outcome>` for a stage that belongs to one workflow. `outcome` is `any` when the stage has one successor whatever the verdict. A value is `{command, why}`: `command` is what the reader runs next, or `null` when the stage hands off to a person (`human`) or to a decision (`decide`). Fields `human` and `decide` carry the sentence a report prints instead of a command. Nothing here calls a tool: it is the table `crew-router.mdc` routes and `crew-orchestrator.mdc` sequences.

build.spec.drafted.why: the spec is written and awaits approval

build.implement.all_passed.why: every task passed, so the change is reviewed before it is committed

build.implement.failed.decide: retry the failed tasks, skip them, or stop here
build.implement.failed.why: a failed task is the user's call, never an automatic retry

build.review.block.why: a blocking finding is resolved before the change is committed

build.review.pass.why: nothing blocks, so the change is shipped: committed and opened as a draft PR

build.review.warn.why: attention findings do not block, so the change is shipped: committed and opened as a draft PR

build.review.pr.human: paste the bodies from `comments.md` onto the PR; nothing was posted
build.review.pr.why: a PR review's findings are about someone else's branch, so a person posts them

build.review.spec.human: approve the revised SPEC.md (Gate 1), then run `crew implement`.
build.review.spec.why: a spec review revises the plan, and only the user can approve it

build.review.idea.why: an idea review strengthens the proposal, which the next step turns into a spec

build.commit.committed.why: the commit exists and the branch is pushed as a draft PR

build.open-pr.opened.why: the draft PR is open and review comments arrive there; a PR merged into a base other than the default branch is merged but not landed there, and `crew ls --all` shows it as `landed: no`

respond.address-pr.applied.why: the approved edits are committed before any thread is answered

respond.push.pushed.why: the pushed fixes are reviewed; the resolver cannot dispatch the inline-only reviewer
